intro: Lesson 20. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: كَلَّآ إِنَّ كِتَٰبَ ٱلْفُجَّارِ لَفِى سِجِّينٍۢ (٧) وَمَآ أَدْرَىٰكَ مَا سِجِّينٌۭ (٨) كِتَٰبٌۭ مَّرْقُومٌۭ (٩) وَيْلٌۭ يَوْمَئِذٍۢ لِّلْمُكَذِّبِينَ (١٠) ٱلَّذِينَ يُكَذِّبُونَ بِيَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ (١١) وَمَا يُكَذِّبُ بِهِۦٓ إِلَّا كُلُّ مُعْتَدٍ أَثِيمٍ (١٢)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: No! Indeed, the record of the wicked is in sijjeen.
And what can make you know what is sijjeen?
It is [their destination recorded in] a register inscribed.
Woe, that Day, to the deniers,
Who deny the Day of Recompense.
And none deny it except every sinful transgressor.

questions.q: Chunk and link Al-Mutaffifin 83:7-12 together, ayah by ayah.
questions.a: The class recites 83:7-12 together without the mushaf.

questions.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 83:7-12 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: Find two hams (whispered) letters in 83:7 to 9.
questions.a: For example: ك and ت in كِتَٰبَ, س in سِجِّينٍۢ, ف in لَفِى.

questions.q: Who are 'every sinful transgressor' (83:12) according to the ayah?
questions.a: Those who deny the Day of Judgement and go beyond limits in sin.
A) The deniers (al-mukadhdhibin). 83:10 to 11: woe to the deniers who deny the Day of Recompense.

questions.q: Think again: Allah says the record of the wicked is in 'sijjin', 'a register inscribed' (83:7 to 9). Why does it matter that our deeds are written?
questions.a: Nothing is forgotten: good and bad deeds are recorded, so we try to fill our record with good.
